findings.title: Blocked-email lookup is case- and whitespace-sensitive, allowing bypass
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` looks up the raw submitted value with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first`, and `set_defaults` never normalizes stored addresses. On the default Postgres setup this comparison is case-sensitive, and surrounding whitespace also matters. A blocked address such as `spammer@example.com` can therefore still register as `Spammer@example.com` or `spammer@example.com ` because the validator finds no record and returns false. Normalize both the stored address and the lookup value (for example with `Email.downcase`/strip), and enforce that normalization on write, including the unique constraint, so the block cannot be bypassed by casing or whitespace.

findings.title: should_block? mutates the record during validation and is not atomic
findings.body: `BlockedEmail.should_block?` performs `record.match_count += 1` and `record.save` every time it is called, but it is called from `EmailValidator`, so it runs during validation rather than only when a signup actually fails. In `UsersController#create`, `user.valid?` (line 168) is followed by `user.save` (line 172), so a single blocked signup attempt invokes it twice and increments `match_count` twice; any other `valid?` call also increments it. The read/modify/write is also racy, so concurrent checks lose increments. This makes `match_count`/`last_match_at` unreliable and adds database writes to validation. Record the match once at the point of the blocked signup, and use an atomic counter update such as `increment_counter`/`update_counters`.

findings.title: Migration added without updating db/schema.rb
findings.body: The PR creates the `blocked_emails` table in a migration but does not update `db/schema.rb`. Rails test and development databases are normally loaded from `schema.rb`, so the new `BlockedEmail` model and specs will fail with a missing `blocked_emails` table unless the test setup happens to run migrations. Regenerate and commit `db/schema.rb` with the new table and unique email index.
